verdict.rationale: Gaudi 3 is an AI accelerator, so asking about a GPU-compute toolchain is a fair question for this kind of product. However, nothing in the evidence shows CUDA or ROCm/HIP documentation listing Gaudi 3 as a supported target. The docs describe Intel's own Gaudi software stack (PyTorch, DeepSpeed, vLLM, Docker images) and tools for migrating GPU-based models, which is an adjacent capability, not the CUDA/ROCm support the story names.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship GPU-compute workloads on the vendor's toolchain — CUDA or ROCm/HIP documentation lists this part as a supported target
